meta.title: WaterUI — Cross-platform UI for Rust
meta.description: Write once, apply everywhere. WaterUI is a UI framework for Rust: one view tree that becomes native controls on Apple platforms and is drawn by its own renderer, Hydrolysis, everywhere else, Android included.

hero.lead: WaterUI is a UI framework for Rust. Write a view once: it becomes UIKit and AppKit controls on Apple platforms, and Hydrolysis draws it on the GPU everywhere else, Android included.
hero.figure: One struct, rendered by each officially supported backend. These are captures of the example, not mockups.

state.label: State
state.title: Change one value. Touch one view.
state.lead: State is plain values. There is no virtual tree to diff, and changing one string never rebuilds the subtree around it.

binding.title: Binding<T> is mutable state
binding.body: Put a value in a Binding and hand it to views. Any view that reads it updates when it changes.

computed.title: Computed<T> is derived state
computed.body: Map a Binding into a Computed. Signal-aware APIs accept either, and only their readers update.

collections.title: Collections diff by identity
collections.body: Give List or ForEach a reactive collection of Identifiable items and membership changes are diffed by id.

state.figureCounter: The counter from the figure: one Binding, one reader, one writer.

figure.caption: Each view that does work for the change flashes. An illustration of the update model.

kit.title: WaterKit
kit.lead: The platform services around the UI: one Rust API per capability, a native implementation on each platform.
kit.figure: WaterKit, one Rust API per capability

testing.title: Testing
testing.lead: Accessibility-first tests run under plain cargo test against the Hydrolysis renderer. No simulator, no device. Interactions are assertions, and every wait pumps to quiescence instead of sleeping.
testing.figure: A semantic test, run by cargo test

notes.assert: asserts on the state, not on pixels

previews.lead: Any function marked #[preview] renders to an image without launching the app, and the same preview runs semantic interaction tests.

backends.label: Backends
backends.lead: Apple maps each view onto UIKit and AppKit. Hydrolysis draws the same view tree itself, on the GPU, everywhere else: Android, the desktop and the web.
backends.experimentalNote: Usable and tested nightly, but not yet held to the same bar.

hydrolysis.name: Hydrolysis
hydrolysis.renders: WaterUI's own GPU renderer, through wgpu

engine.label: Rendering
engine.title: Hydrolysis draws the tree itself.
engine.lead: WaterUI's own renderer. It draws the complete retained view tree on the GPU, from one codebase, wherever there is no native toolkit to map onto, or wherever you would rather not use one.

gpu.title: The whole tree, on the GPU
gpu.body: Every view is drawn through wgpu. There is no CPU fallback to quietly take over.

platforms.title: Desktop, web and Android
platforms.body: macOS, Windows and Linux windows, the browser through WebGPU, and Android through its own host.

frames.title: Budgeted for 120 Hz
frames.body: Frames are budgeted for 120 Hz displays, and a window with nothing to change draws nothing.

accessibility.title: Tested through its accessibility tree
accessibility.body: waterui-testing queries the accessibility tree Hydrolysis builds, so every UI test is also an accessibility test.

themes.title: Themes are packages
themes.body: Hydrolysis carries no widget style of its own. Material 3 ships as a separate package.

cherenkov.title: Cherenkov, the engine built for it.
cherenkov.lead: A GPU 2D engine designed around WaterUI's fine-grained reactivity and around current GPUs. It takes WaterUI's signals as its own inputs, so a change costs what it touches, not what is on screen.
cherenkov.status: On the dev channel Hydrolysis renders through Cherenkov; the stable 0.5 release still renders through Vello. Carrying WaterUI's signals straight into Cherenkov's value slots is in progress.

slots.title: Signals become engine operands
slots.body: A bound value is a slot in the engine. When it changes, only the recorded commands that read it are regenerated; the rest of the frame is reused.

animation.title: Animation on the render thread
animation.body: A change made with .animation() reaches the engine as is. The render thread interpolates it, so a frame's cost follows what is moving, not the size of the scene.

colour.title: Built for current displays
colour.body: Rendering happens in linear, extended-range colour with a wide-gamut working space, and each window negotiates HDR or wide-gamut output with its display.

figure.caption: A corner radius bound to a signal. Moving it touches only the commands that read it. An illustration of the engine's value slots.
